claims.head: Carolina likes this matchup at home
claims.body: At home, Carolina’s P3 (Reilly, Gostisbehere) has spent 48% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ third lines. With no line matching it would be about 26%. Tonight Washington’s usual third line is Jenner, Beauvillier, Sourdif.

notes.text: R. Sandin has not played this season. T. Liljegren is in his usual spot beside M. Fehérváry. That pair is getting 7:02 a game at 5-on-5, down from 8:00 with Sandin. M. Roy has moved into Liljegren’s old spot beside J. Chychrun.

S. Jarvis has not played this season. W. Carrier is in his usual spot beside S. Aho and A. Svechnikov, up from fourth-line minutes last season. That line is getting 9:15 a game at 5-on-5, down from 10:44 with Jarvis. J. Kotkaniemi has moved into Carrier’s old spot beside M. Jankowski and E. Robinson.
L. Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: J. Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 68% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 61 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by N. Ehlers (15 of 18 changes).

CAR.head: Carolina has nearly everything going for it
CAR.body: Carolina has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Washington can make a game of it if it gets to the dangerous areas.

WSH.head: Washington has its work cut out
WSH.body: Carolina has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Washington could still pull it off if it gets to the dangerous areas, but it might need a miracle.
